chapter: Haiti, Artie Shaw and Los Angeles work
title: Operation Entertainment with Terry Gibbs
summary: The Chuck Barris show took bands to army camps for two seasons and was killed by sponsors' distaste for the Vietnam War.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: went to New York, and Bobby hired Grady and I agreed to do the Today Show with us, we did the Today Show. And I was very happy to do this, and then I went back to California and re-joined Terry Gibbs on this Operation Entertainment. A very supersat good band. I don't know whether I told you, but the super saxes, that was just about ---that was our sax section on Terry's band. I mentioned that before, it was an excellent band. I enjoyed it.

Operation Entertainment was a show put together by Chuck Barris. Now, you know who Chuck Barris is. He's the Dating Game, the Mating Game, everything this man touched turned to gold. Everyone but the one Operation Entertainment, naturally. We did it for two seasons any way.
was it a syndicated TV series? (Inaudible).

Yeah. Now, the format was similar to the Bob Hope Christmas Show. We would go to various army camps, and do shows there, and they'd have the greatest acts in show business. You know, the money was no object. We had the greatest acts in show business every -- we had Louie Armstrong group, Phil Harris, Florence Henderson, just everybody in show business. But the war -- that was a very unpopular war, this Vietnam war, and nobody -- no sponsor really wanted to be identified with anything concerning this war. So I think this is what really just killed the show.
But it was a very good show, and an enjoyable show because it was just such a wonderful band. Yeah.
You did that for two years? (Inaudible).
